MA and PhD Supervision
The Political Science department at NIU has a long and prestigious tradition of Masters and PhD level graduate training. Our students go onto successful careers in academia, public service, etc all over the world.
I am particularly interested in working with students focused on global environmental issues including those from Southeast Asia and the rest of the developing. Please get in touch prior to applying if you have interest in joining our program or working directly with me as a supervisor.

title: Student Research
text:
Undergraduate Research

Most semesters I oversee an undergraduate research lab. Despite the corny name the lab endeavors to take on ambitious empirical research focused on using the tools of social science to improve the natural environment. I am always looking for motivated undergraduate students interested in contributing. If you are interested in joining, as either a research assistant or independent researcher, please email or stop by office hours.

title: Research
text:
Overview
My research focuses on the politics of environmental behavior across multiple scales and across various issue areas. It applies political science frameworks to understanding the social a causes of environmental problems, focusing on what motivates actors to contribute to environmental protection. It begins with an assumption that we have sufficient scientific knowledge and viable solutions to most environmental challenges, political barriers remain the primary obstacle to progress. I examine these barriers across multiple levels of analysis using rigorous methods, including experiments, text-as-data techniques, and traditional large-N analysis. I also frequently collaborate with scholars in fields such as social psychology, communication, ecology, and geology to address problems more comprehensively. This interdisciplinary approach allows me to bridge academic divides and contribute insights that inform both political scientists and the broader environmental community.

title: Research
text:
Ongoing Research Projects


Public Preferences for Global Cooperation
My book attempts to understand public attitudes around to world toward global environmental cooperation, like the Paris Agreement. While canonical models suggest issues like climate change are the ultimate collective action problem, the public doesn’t seem to think so. A trove of observational and experimental studies show that individuals are overwhelming supportive of cooperative efforts and don’t think about these issues in terms of guarantees of reciprocity. The book takes a deep dive into these issues and tries to understand how individuals around the world can drive more effective global environmental governance.


Understanding Sustainability Communications using Textual Data
Textual data is underutilized in the study of environmental politics. In a series of projects I’m working on with varios co-authors this work uses multiple text-as-data techniques to understand how actors, like local governments and private governance actors,actually communicate about sustainability issues.


Accountability and Action in Southeast Asian Environmental Politics
Our planet’s path to environmental sustainabilty surely runs through Southeast Asia. No other region in the world better exemplifies the challenges and opportunities
If you are interested in getting involved in these projects or hearing more please do not hesitate to reach out to me

Dr. Colin Kuehl is an Associate Professor in the Department of Political Science and Institute for the Study of the Environment Sustainability and Energy at Northern Illinois University where is also affiliated with the Center for Southeast Asian Studies.
For the Spring 2026 semester he is a Visiting Scholar at Northwestern University Department of Political Science and Summer 2026 will be a Visiting Professor at the School of Public Policy at Chiang Mai University in Thailand.
Dr. Kuehl’s scholarship focuses the politics of environmental behavior. He researches broad question across different political domains and levels of analysis, from motivating individuals to conserve water to what makes countries more likely to ratify multi-lateral environmental agreements, using a wide variety of methodological approachs. His work has been published in Environmental Politics,Nature Sustainability, The Journal of Policy Analysis and Management, Science Communication, and other highly regarded outlets. He is currently working on a book project focused on individual attitudes toward global environmental cooperation.
Colin was born and raised in small-town northeast Oregon and received his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 2017. In his free time he likes to drink coffee, watch soccer (#ynwa), and go on road trips with with his wife, two daughters, and dog.
